Cleaning Data

Setup

Setting up the libraries.

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(readr)

Import

Importing the raw beverage data.

bev_raw <- read_csv("data-original/bev-raw.csv")

Cleaning columns

Selecting the columns relevant to analysis.

bev_col <- bev_raw |>
  select(
    `Taxpayer Number`,
    `Location Number`,
    `Location Name`,
    `Location Address`,
    `Location City`,
    `Location Zip`,
    `Obligation End Date`,
    `Beer Receipts`,
    `Wine Receipts`,
    `Liquor Receipts`,
    `Total Receipts`
  ) |>
  clean_names()

bev_col

Convert data types

Fixing the data types.

bev_clean <- bev_col |>
  mutate(
    date = mdy(obligation_end_date),
    year = year(date),
    location_zip = as.character(location_zip),
    beer_receipts = as.numeric(gsub("[,$]", "", beer_receipts)),
    wine_receipts = as.numeric(gsub("[,$]", "", wine_receipts)),
    liquor_receipts = as.numeric(gsub("[,$]", "", liquor_receipts)),
    total_receipts = as.numeric(gsub("[,$]", "", total_receipts))
  ) |>
  filter(year != 2026)

bev_clean

Export

Export the cleaned dataset.

write_rds(bev_clean, "data-processed/bev_clean.rds")

The use of gsub() in this notebook was informed by this website after my code failed to run and I tried numerous methods to change my code. The original problem was different but I ended up forgetting to switch this back to parse_number().
